Very, very bad experience. Honestly, I’m so glad I didn’t choose this clinic for my surgery.

I was planning to travel all the way from Toronto to have my breast augmentation done with them. I messaged the clinic first, and it took them several days just to respond. Then I called because I had questions about the surgery and wanted to understand the process before traveling to another city.

The woman who answered the phone was unbelievably rude. She clearly did not want to communicate in English, and the way she spoke to me was extremely disrespectful and unprofessional. When I asked her questions about the surgery process, she basically said, “I don’t know. Book an appointment online and come to the clinic in person.” Then she literally hung up the phone while I was still talking.

Seriously? This is how you speak to someone who is considering traveling from Toronto and trusting your clinic with a major surgery?

Thank God I didn’t go there. I ended up finding a much better surgeon with a beautiful, professional clinic in Westmount, and the difference in how I was treated was huge.

This clinic seriously needs to train its staff on how to speak to patients and potential clients. Customer service is not optional, especially when you work in cosmetic surgery. The entire team should receive proper professional training on how to communicate with people. My first impression was terrible, and after that phone call, I would never consider having surgery there.

one_star_reviews.text:
One of the most heartless customer service experiences I have ever had.

My brother passed away suddenly in British Columbia. After finally being able to bring him home to Edson, we were trying to prepare for his funeral and burial. Because of how sudden everything was, there was obviously no opportunity to preorder flowers.

We went into this florist and simply asked whether they happened to have any carnations available that they could spare.

Instead of kindness, the woman working told us that we “should have preordered.”

We explained that my brother had suddenly passed away and that we had only just been able to get him home to Edson. Her response was a condescending, “Good luck finding any in town.” That was it. No “I’m sorry for your loss.” No compassion. No attempt to help. Not even basic courtesy.

To be clear, I would never fault a florist for not having a particular flower in stock. That is completely understandable. What is not understandable is speaking to a grieving family with such coldness after they have just explained that they are trying to bury their brother.

We did not walk in demanding anything. We asked a simple question.
There are certain situations where a little humanity should come naturally. This should have been one of them.
I left absolutely disgusted by the way we were treated. I will never forget the complete lack of empathy shown to my family during one of the worst days of our lives.

I should not have to risk damage to an expensive vehicle because a known maintenance problem has been left unresolved for months.

This is unacceptable and extremely frustrating.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing rental experience
What initially seemed like a great rental turned into a very frustrating experience.
When we moved in, the property was not in a reasonably clean condition. We found leftover food in the refrigerator and freezer, used toilet paper on the toilet seat, insects in the bathtub, garbage, and personal belongings from the previous tenant throughout the kitchen. We immediately reported the situation by email and provided photos. Since we had arrived late from another city, we had to stay at a hotel that night.
Despite our request for the property to be properly cleaned first thing the following morning, assistance did not arrive until around 3:00 p.m., after we followed up by phone. Very little cleaning was actually completed, and we had to deal with many of the previous tenant's belongings ourselves. We were also told that the cleaning we had to do ourselves would be reimbursed, but this did not happen.
Additional issues followed, including a loose shower, mold, hot water problems, and a silverfish infestation throughout the house. Some of our concerns received little or no follow-up. There was also no move-in inspection, despite one being included in the lease.
Our main concern was not that the property had issues — problems can happen — but the **lack of communication, timely response, and follow-through in addressing them**.
We cannot comment on what the property owners were aware of, as we do not have that information. However, based on our experience with the property management, **we would not recommend RE/MAX for property management services**. We expected a properly prepared rental and reasonable support when issues arose, and unfortunately, that was not our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Uniti - Avoid at All Costs
1 Star — Current Resident
The overall condition, safety, and management of this building have declined drastically since Uniti took over, turning it into the worst place I have ever lived. For the exorbitant rent charged, the living conditions are completely unacceptable.
Severe Safety & Security Risks: The building is entirely unsafe. We deal with hovering individuals and substance use issues throughout the property—making it feel less like a secure apartment and more like the side of the road. There are no security guards, and when residents raise valid safety concerns, management simply tells us to "call 911."
Rampant Theft & Parcel Loss: Couriers and parcels are regularly stolen from the building with zero support, cameras, or preventative action from management.
Completely Broken Infrastructure: This is an 18-floor high-rise, yet the elevators are broken for ages, leaving residents stranded. Parking is a constant headache: despite paying separately for assigned stalls, our designated spots are frequently occupied by unauthorized vehicles and unfamiliar people staying in the garage.
Neglected Amenities & Overpriced Services: The gym is completely unsanitary with empty supply stocks, and the laundry rates are unjustifiably higher than surrounding buildings.
Abysmal Management: There is a constant revolving door of incompetent building managers, zero customer service, and an absolute lack of respect for families and long-term tenants.
Save your money, protect your safety, and look elsewhere. Evacuate this building if you can—I would give it 0/5 stars if Google allowed it.

Very disappointing experience so far

I have been living in this building for about 6 years. While parts of my tenancy in the past have been comfortable, the overall condition and management of the property have declined significantly, particularly over the last year.

For the quality of the renovations and the current condition of the building, I find the rent extremely overpriced. There are also recurring issues with unhoused individuals and people struggling with substance use being present around the property and common areas. At times, this has made the building feel uncomfortable and unsafe.

There also seems to be a general lack of care and oversight when it comes to the property. Garbage is frequently left throughout the building, the common areas often smell terrible, and the overall cleanliness and upkeep have noticeably declined.

Management is another major issue. There has been a constant revolving door of building managers, making it difficult to know who is actually responsible for addressing concerns. As I’m writing this review, there is currently no building manager.

Getting important maintenance issues addressed can take an unreasonable amount of time. For example, MOLD and our SINKING CELING  took approximately 6 months to be dealt with. During that time, it was extremely toxic and disruptive, making it difficult to use properly or even rest comfortably.

There have also been ongoing concerns with mold and other important maintenance issues, along with frequent elevator problems. Parking is another recurring frustration. Tenants pay separately for assigned parking spaces, yet my designated spot has frequently been occupied by other vehicles. On some occasions, unfamiliar individuals have also been staying in the parking area.

Overall, I feel there has been a noticeable decline in cleanliness, maintenance, security, and general care for the property. Since Uniti took over, the building has steadily gone downhill in my experience.

I’m still living here, so this isn’t a review from someone who moved out years ago. This is based on my current experience as a resident.

For the amount of rent being charged, I would expect significantly better management, maintenance, cleanliness, and security.
I would give it 0/5 if I could

————————

UPDATE

The Apartment building is an absolute dump.
Me and my GF were promised to have mold testing done and properly investigated however they never follow though. Truly shady people with 0 regard for their residents. Garbage, filth everywhere’. Our floor has not been vacuumed in over a month.

Would not recommend Chelsea Estates or UnitiiPM. I lived there for over 18 months and had no issues as a tenant. On the day I moved out, a box of belongings was stolen from outside the elevators. I reported it immediately and was told by onsite management that they could see someone taking it on CCTV and would follow up. After weeks of emails, calls and escalations, no meaningful action was taken and management eventually closed the matter.

I also spent weeks trying to find out what had happened to my $250 security deposit. I was only recently provided with a Statement of Account dated July 15, which I had never previously received. It simply showed a $0 balance and did not list any deductions. I was then told, nearly two months after moving out, that my entire $250 deposit had apparently been used for cleaning charges. I am still waiting for the supporting documentation.

Extremely poor communication and accountability when something actually goes wrong.

Between business and personal we make thousands of on line purchases of which 99% are good, this however was one of the very worst. I purchased the customized frame, fork, and ride chain-stay armour and two boxed of extra film. It arrived in a protective box and all looked ok, but I did not like the matte finish so I returned it and purchased the gloss version along with more product, and this is where it fell apart. It took a week to get an email answer from Ayden at ride wrap and he told me they would not ship a new one until an investigation was done, only after stating my case to them did they finally send it (remember 5-7 days to get any emails from ride wrap so resolving something takes a long time). Had it not been for the high re stocking fee I would have returned it all and purchased 3m automotive wrap or wrap from another company, even ordering custom wrap or cutting myself would have been far better. I bought my new Epic bike in mid June, ordered ride wrap a few days later and did not get it wrapped or to ride it until Aug 21. I missed two bike trips and two months of riding in our already short season because of this product. They need a faster form of communication for customers who have issues with product or shipping. My son has an opioid addiction, we almost lost him last year. He was 11 months clean and relapsed in June. I was desperate as we are when our children relapse and was actively searching for a good quality treatment that had availability immediately. I talked to Into Action and they sounded like they had an OK program and have been around for a long time. I choose to go with hirer priced program they offered “Inspire” in White Rock because they had 3 one on one counselling sessions a week and offered a few other things that the lower priced programs did not,  I felt my son would do better with the extras. I also ASSUMED the rooms and food would be better, they were not. The food is being delivered every day, not cooked in house, which is a huge surprise for my son, not the quality we expected.

They picked him up and took him to the home. Once he arrived, they made him sign their contracts, he was so high he was not capable reading or signing anything. Their contract states they were supposed to search his items, which they did not and left stuff on him, also in the contract was that they took his phone away for 7 days (very important part) on day 5 he calls me BECAUSE THEY GAVE HIM HIS PHONE, and says he is leaving, they have basically left him in a room for days detoxing by himself. So, he leaves…… I called them for my refund of $20,500, they said that my son signed a contract stating that they hold my money for 365 days and I had to wait this waiting period, but he is welcome back anytime. How can they have an intoxicated addict sign a financial contract, he did not pay for the treatment. I scaped together all that money and now paying interest on it while they hold it and MAKE interest on it!! He refuses to go back because of his treatment there and I cannot afford to send him anywhere else. They are supposed to be helping these addicts, that is the opposite of what they are doing. They have lost sight of what they are supposed to be doing , all they care about is the money!!

The plants and shrubs were planted haphazardly, without equal spacing, and some plants not suited to full sun were placed in direct sunlight. Despite thorough watering, several dried out and died.

The soil they installed was full of glass fragments, with an incorrect pH and very few nutrients. My grass seed barely sprouted, and I had to correct the situation myself with fertilizer and other products.

When they were building the fountain, they cut concrete without adequate protection. I had even brought them a hose to minimize dust. They only used it for a few minutes, then continued cutting without water. Cement and concrete dust are very harmful to health when inhaled, which makes this way of working particularly concerning. As a result, dust and concrete residue ended up everywhere, including in my swimming pool, affecting my filters and the water quality.

I had also just had a beautiful new fence installed, which ended up covered in dust. I spent several hours cleaning the fence, the furniture, and the surrounding area, in addition to having to pick up cement residue from my pool for a good part of the summer. I even received complaints from neighbors about all the dust.

For the size and cost of the project, I expected much more care and professionalism. Unfortunately, I had to dedicate a huge amount of time to cleaning up and fixing problems that could have been avoided.

We had a terrible experience with Myers Cadillac. We were in town for a wedding, when he vehicle stopped working on the Queensway. We had our car taken to the dealership after Canadian Tire said it could be a computer issue. It wasn’t, it was our alternator, which we had replaced with Myers. Our bill was 2,300, which isn’t even the part that upsets us. We understand the cost of owning a car, and had no issues paying the bill. Our first issue was with Dave, the service guy who quoted us 2,500 and when we pushed back a bit to understand he was condescending and said “well, you know.. bolts do need to be removed”. My husband is a senior foreman in renewable energy and an expert field advisor.. he is intelligent and works with tools, his push back wasn’t with the cost it was a genuine desire to understand the required services.

We agree to the service, leave our car. We had the service manager reach out, I’m guessing it’s because I was trying to use the chat to contact the dealership because their phones were down. Once he reached out, I just let him know that if they want future business, it’s probably a bad idea for your service guys to be unfriendly and rude. The service manager was kind enough and was prompt with responses.

Once we picked up our car, we noticed a Tim Hortons cop was left in the cup holder. We don’t drink Tim Hortons, and the cup was covered in oil (I’m assuming, one of the workers must have accidentally left it in the car). The issue with that, is the cup bottom fell apart and our cup holders are not soaked with old coffee and milk… which the smell has been difficult to get out.

Then, we noticed our front seat has a small tear in the leather, which was not there when we left the car. I’m assuming they didn’t cover the seats of the steering when working on the car, because the steering wheel was covered in oil and dirt.

This service for a Cadillac dealership is completely unacceptable.

I’m very disappointed with my experience at Milano Bags and Baggage. I purchased a small luggage that was on sale. I originally wanted the blue color, but I was told by the sales lady that they did not have blue available, so I chose a different color instead.
Later, when I passed by the store again, I saw that they had a blue one on display, also on sale. I asked the same sales lady if I could exchange my luggage for the blue one, and I was told yes. Based on that assurance, I came back with the luggage I had purchased.
However, when I returned, I was suddenly told that they could not do the exchange because the blue luggage had already been sold to someone else. I was extremely frustrated because I was given different information at different times.
The resolution they offered was that they would order another blue luggage for me and asked me to come back after two weeks. I agreed and waited.
After two weeks, I came back expecting the luggage they had promised, only to be told that they did not have the luggage they promised to order. Instead, they offered me a completely different style that was not what I wanted.
They also told me that I could choose another luggage as a replacement, but I would have to pay the additional amount if the replacement luggage was more expensive than what I originally purchased. I found this very frustrating because I was being asked to pay extra for an alternative after the original exchange and special order were not properly handled.
What makes this experience even more disappointing is that they would not offer a refund or another reasonable solution, despite the situation resulting from their own changing information and promises.
I understand that mistakes can happen, but what matters is how a business handles those mistakes. In this case, I felt that my concerns were not taken seriously and that the responsibility was ultimately placed on me as the customer.
To other customers: please make sure you are completely certain about the product and exchange policy before purchasing. I personally would be very cautious about relying on verbal promises regarding exchanges or special orders. If something is promised to you, I strongly recommend getting it in writing.
I hope management takes this feedback seriously and improves their customer service, communication, and handling of situations like this. I would have appreciated a fair and honest resolution rather than being given promises that were ultimately not fulfilled.

If I could leave 0 or negative stars, I would.
Our experience was absolutely horrible.
A little history so you know why we ended up there.
My wife’s 2018 Traverse was hit in a parking lot while on vacation in BC. Ripped the bottom corner of the rear hatch open. Wide enough that you could reach your arm in to the shoulder.
I dropped it off for an estimate and was told it was unsafe to drive due to exhaust emissions. They gave us a rental. A Toyota RAV 4 base model. Nothing against the Toyota but not close to the level of vehicle we dropped off.
In communications with the shop,after several requests for simple inquiries, I was never allowed to speak with a shop manager.
The day we were told we could pick up the vehicle, we were told the battery was dead and we needed to bring a new one.They claimed “no fault”. No reimbursement was provided or even offered. Intact insurance would not cover it either.
After living with the “repaired” vehicle for a week or so, we found the rear hatch squeeked and each time we used the rear window washer, it would blow the fuse. We returned it to rectify. They adjusted the hatch but claimed “no fault” for the washer issue.
Further and finally, while raising the hatch remotely, one of the struts fell from its connecting point on the hatch and smashed the tail light. We returned the vehicle once more and guess what?! They claimed “no fault” even though, they had the entire hatch off the vehicle.
Zero to negative stars. Do not recommend.
Avoid.

one_star_reviews.text:
Proceed With Caution

Based on our experience, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering renting from this property management company think very carefully before doing so.

The most disappointing aspect has been the complete lack of compassion, empathy, and basic human understanding shown toward tenants and their individual circumstances. There seems to be very little consideration for the fact that the people living in these buildings are actual human beings, many of whom are seniors, families, and vulnerable individuals who deserve to be treated with dignity and respect.

A property management company should understand that being a landlord is more than collecting rent and enforcing rules. It also requires compassion, communication, reasonable judgment, and humanity — particularly when dealing with vulnerable residents and difficult family circumstances.

Unfortunately, our experience has left us with the impression that those qualities are seriously lacking here.

If you are considering renting from this company, I would strongly encourage you to do your research, speak with current or former tenants, and consider whether this is the type of management company you want responsible for your home.

A home should feel like a safe place to live, not a place where tenants feel scrutinized, unsupported, or treated as an inconvenience.

A Response to KPM Kingsway Property Management’s Statement

The response provided by management sounds compassionate and responsible on the surface, but unfortunately it avoids the central issue.

No one is suggesting that property management should ignore legitimate safety concerns or complaints from residents. Of course management has responsibilities to the entire building.

The concern is where reasonable concern ends and unnecessary interference in a tenant’s personal life begins.

There is a significant difference between responding to a resident who is actually in distress, lost, injured, creating a safety issue, or otherwise requiring assistance — and repeatedly scrutinizing a resident simply because management has decided that their personal circumstances mean they should not be doing something independently.

What is particularly concerning is the repeated use of words such as “intervention,” “additional support,” “meaningful improvement,” and “appropriate parties” without clearly identifying what actual behaviour or incident required intervention in the first place.

Property management companies are not medical professionals, and a tenant’s medical diagnosis should not become a blanket justification for restricting their independence or treating ordinary activities as inherently problematic.

If there is a legitimate safety concern, then address the specific conduct or incident that created that concern. Be factual. Be reasonable. Communicate with the appropriate people. And, above all, approach vulnerable residents with dignity.

What is disappointing about this response is that it spends several paragraphs explaining how compassionate and empathetic management believes itself to be, rather than addressing the very real concern that prompted the criticism in the first place.

Compassion isn’t simply saying that you have it. It is demonstrated by how you treat people when circumstances are difficult.

Tenants are not merely leases, units and monthly rent payments. They are people, and many will eventually be elderly, disabled, vulnerable, or dealing with circumstances that require understanding rather than unnecessary scrutiny.

A responsible property management company should know the difference between protecting a resident and unnecessarily policing one.

That distinction matters.

⚠️ Extremely disappointing experience

I came here because I genuinely wanted to adopt a dog and give an animal a good home. I first arrived around 9 AM because Google said the place was open, only to find out that 9 AM was apparently for the clinic and not adoptions. I was told to come back at 12, so I did exactly that.

When I came back, I called and was told that I would need to come another day and that they would call me to make an appointment. Then, while I was waiting and texting my mother, a staff member came outside and started questioning us about what we were doing there, where we lived, and other personal information. My brother was also questioned.

What made the experience especially upsetting was that I felt we were being treated with suspicion based on our appearance. We are Arab, and the way we were questioned made me feel like we were being treated as if we were there to steal a dog rather than people genuinely trying to adopt one. We were even told that our parents needed to be there because apparently they didn't believe we had a home.

On top of that, staff took pictures of our vehicle/license plate, which made the whole situation feel even more uncomfortable and suspicious.

If there are specific requirements for adoption, that's completely understandable. But those requirements should be communicated clearly and respectfully to everyone. People who come to adopt an animal are there because they care about animals and want to give one a home. Making people feel unwelcome, suspicious, or judged because of their appearance is unacceptable.

I left feeling extremely disappointed and uncomfortable. I hope management takes this seriously and looks into how potential adopters are being treated.

Dryers that don't work or only half work, and washing machines that leave clothes dirty. Flies coming out of the sinks in the residents' rooms, and lights that only half work. 1) There's no personal trainer.
2) The food is awful, nothing like what they show on the website (gourmet food). On Sundays, they give us all the leftovers from the week. Cooked fish on Monday, and they give it back on Sunday.

3) We can't go for walks in the woods except at the top of a small hill where there's a completely wrecked cabin.
4) We can't watch TV except on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays from 8:00 to 10:30, and if the movie isn't finished, the staff turns off the TV.

5) We can't listen to music except in the evening in our rooms or on weekends.
6) We have to do a major cleaning of the building every Saturday, cleaning the toilets, etc.
7) They have a store for residents, but the prices are really expensive. And you have to hide your things because a lot of things disappear.

8) The hockey and basketball courts are completely destroyed; the hockey equipment is all broken.
9) There are four cats living in the building; there's cat litter everywhere, not cleaned up, and poop next to the litter boxes.

I definitely advise against this place.

one_star_reviews.text:
Endless wait, hidden fees, and a vehicle with flat tire

I booked with Routes through EconomyBookings because they offered the best rate near Montreal Airport. Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing.

The wait at the counter is extremely long: despite having four employees working, the check-in process seemed to take about 45 minutes per customer. The process is also unnecessarily complicated, with a contract sent by email requiring multiple signatures and being difficult to review on a phone.

I was also informed at check-in that there was an additional $21 per day fee if I planned to drive into Ontario. This fee was not clearly displayed when booking and was instead buried in the fine print of the confirmation — which is rather ironic considering their vehicles are themselves registered in Ontario.

The Nissan Rogue I was given had a tire that was losing air. They simply inflated it again and insisted that I take the vehicle. A few minutes after leaving, the tire started losing air again. I had to return to the rental office, wait again, and was eventually given a lower-category vehicle with no compensation.

The return process went smoothly, but it has to be done during business hours, which limits flexibility, and I never received any confirmation afterward that the vehicle had been properly returned. I also heard several customers complaining about how the airport shuttle system operates.

The only positive point was that the staff were friendly. That said, between the long wait, the lack of transparency regarding fees, and the issue with the vehicle, I would not rent from Routes again and would not recommend this location.

I wish I could give this place a negative rating. This has been one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had with a repair shop.

My car was with them for almost a month while I had a rental. When I went to pick it up, the work still wasn’t properly finished. They asked me to come back once more to complete the remaining work, and I agreed because I trusted them.

Unfortunately, that was only the beginning. The repairs were not completed properly even though they charged my insurance over $4,000. I originally wasn’t even planning to have the repairs handled through insurance, but I was assured that going through insurance would allow the job to be done properly.

After getting my car back, I spent approximately another month going back almost every week trying to get the issues corrected. Every time there seemed to be another excuse — parts weren’t available, something still needed to be ordered, or I needed to come back another time. After all those visits, the problems still weren’t properly resolved, and I even noticed additional damage to my car.

Communication throughout the process was extremely disappointing. From my experience, I felt like there was much more attention given to getting the insurance payment than making sure I was satisfied with the quality of the repair afterward.

I could write much more about everything that happened, but this is the short version. Based on my personal experience, I would absolutely not recommend this shop for vehicle repairs, especially insurance-related repairs.

one_star_reviews.text:
We lived in this building for a year...

The conditions were so terrible that we left a month before the end of our lease...

There are three elevators, at least one of which is always broken and the management has no desire to fix it. Often the second elevator would break down and only one elevator would remain...

Imagine there was only one elevator for 300 units and in this situation the minimum waiting time for the elevator was 30 minutes...

We sent email to management many times and saying that just as your money is valuable to you, our time is also valuable to us, so please fix the elevators that we don't have to wait in line for half an hour for the elevator, but the management never responded...

The pool and sauna were usually broken and unusable and the sauna was broken for about four months in that year...

When we visited the building, they told that there is two BBQ on the roof top, but there was only physical BBQ and they never connected gas to it and it was unusable...

The parking lot was always full of garbage and we almost never seen it being cleaned...

request for repairs inside the unit were very delayed and took between one and two weeks...

The only thing that was done on time was sending renew lease 😕😂

I would never recommend this building...

one_star_reviews.text:
George will sell you products that don’t work or come damaged and he will not communicate with you. He doesn’t return emails and the general attitude can best be described as aggressively incompetent company wide.

We entrusted qualtech for an expansion last year.

1. Our cheese vat came with a set of knives that didn’t fit the vat so we would only fill it part way. It took 7 months to rectify the situation. They built 2 sets of knives they didn’t even fit along the way. This cost us thousands of dollars.

2. Our tppe draining table which we paid 60k for  came with a divot in it, they don’t bother to examine things - no quality control.

3. The cheese press we bought was manufactured wrong, allowing for side loading of the pistons. It’s been in service 6 months and 6 of the 8 pistons are crooked. I made an initial complaint that the supporting rods to keep the molds inline vertically has between 1 and .75 inches of play which allows the cheese to buckle. I was told experts in France said this was okay. If you’ve made cheese before you know this doesn’t work. The molds need to be tight. It’s so bent now you can’t even use blocks in it. We pulled a 20k press out and threw it into a warehouse.

When something goes wrong they will tell you their experts know it’s right, they won’t fix it. They are too busy trying to sell the next project to bankroll their previous mistakes. To my fellow cheese makers be very wary of them, they will hurt your business financially.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would not trust this service with a good Japanese kitchen knife.

I brought in two knives, including a Japanese Togiharu/Kamata nakiri that was already a very good cutter but had a few rolled/bent spots along the edge. I specifically wanted those spots corrected and the knife sharpened.

After I got home with the freshly sharpened knives, I tested the nakiri. The rolled spots had been straightened, but the knife was substantially duller than before I brought it in. It could not slice ordinary printer paper anywhere along the edge. It had difficulty biting into tomato skin even with significant pressure and required a repeated sawing motion to cut through a tomato. Cutting cabbage also required noticeably more force than before.

I attached a photo taken at home immediately after pickup while testing the freshly sharpened nakiri; it shows the blade pressing deeply into the tomato without breaking the skin.

The Chinese cleaver I brought in was also not consistently sharp from heel to tip and could not cleanly slice paper along the entire edge.

There was also a problem with pickup. We had specifically confirmed a 4:00 PM pickup time. I arrived at 4:00, rang the doorbell three times, called and texted, and received no response. I only got my knives because his daughter happened to come home and went to find him in the backyard. Had she not returned, I have no idea how long I would have been expected to wait.

When Scott handed me the knives, he told me they were “nice and sharp.” Given that the Japanese knife could not cut ordinary printer paper anywhere along its edge when I tested it after the sharpening, I have to question whether he actually tested the knife himself before handing it back and making that statement. A simple paper test would have revealed the problem immediately.

After I sent Scott a photo showing the nakiri pressing deeply into a tomato without cutting through the skin, I requested a refund. He refunded the full $18.

Scott later offered to “put a finer edge” on the Japanese knife. That raises an obvious question: if a finer edge was appropriate for this knife, why wasn’t that edge put on before he handed the knife back to me and described it as “nice and sharp”?

I declined his offer to rework the knife. After receiving a knife back markedly duller than it went in, I was not willing to let it be worked on again.

I now have to take the nakiri to a Japanese-knife specialist in Toronto to have the edge assessed and restored.

A sharpening service should return a knife sharp. A knife that cannot slice printer paper and has to saw through tomato skin should never have been handed back to a customer and described as “nice and sharp.”

one_star_reviews.text:
A very disappointing and uncomfortable experience with Dr. Khulood Murad.

From the moment my appointment began, I felt that the doctor was unfriendly and showed very little empathy or patience.

English is not my first language. Although I can communicate in English, when it comes to medical matters, I need to make sure I fully understand the information being provided. I politely asked the doctor to repeat herself several times because I was having difficulty understanding everything.

To make communication easier, I decided to use the translator on my phone. Unfortunately, instead of receiving patience and understanding, I noticed visible signs of frustration. The doctor repeatedly scratched her head and said “OMG,” which made me feel extremely uncomfortable, nervous, and embarrassed simply because I needed additional help understanding medical information.

At one point, another staff member joined us. I explained that I am an immigrant, that I have been living in Canada for a relatively short time, and that I felt uncomfortable with the way I was being treated.

While I was explaining my concerns, Dr. Murad interrupted and told me that if I did not like her behavior, I could return to my family doctor and request a referral to another gynecologist.

I thanked the other staff member for listening and showing understanding, and I decided to leave.

Canada is a country known for its cultural and linguistic diversity. As a patient, I was not asking for special treatment. I was simply asking for patience, empathy, and respect while trying to understand important information about my own health.

No patient should feel embarrassed or unwelcome simply because English is not their first language.

I left this appointment feeling disappointed, disrespected, and uncomfortable. Based on my personal experience, I would not return to this doctor.

I am sharing this review so that other patients, especially immigrants and those who are not fluent in English, can make an informed decision when choosing their healthcare provider.

Im not sure if I've ever had a worse experience with a physician. Once you go in, be prepared to wait minimum an hour for an appointment. They double book, take people in out of order, and once you're finally in... Dr. Murad spends the whole time trying to leave the room asap. She complains that shes busy, then skims your file because she doesn't even know who you are no matter how many times you've been in. She can't even remember the blood work she sent you for, the medication shes prescribed you, or who shes referred you to. Any concern you have, she dismisses it immediately, and refuses to help. She tells you to look up your concerns online and is very out of touch, rude, and down right mean. She makes you feel stupid, belittled, and tries to make you feel like you're wasting her time.

When I made an appointment to ask about IUDs and share my concerns, she told me "no" blatantly to any pain relief for the procedure and that its fine, and my concerns are not worth while as im being dramatic. She then told me to look it up on my own time, despite the fact i already did and was trying to discuss with her. SHE DOESNT ACTUALLY LISTEN TO WHAT YOU'RE SAYING! She would not listen or even spend any time to talk to me, she refuses to be in a room longer than 5 minutes. She wouldnt even modify or be open to discuss a prescription SHE wrote because she claims to not know anything about the drug. If you dont know the prescription medication, why prescribe it to me??? She makes me cry every time I leave her office, and she takes advantage of patients because they're scared of retaliation. I could seriously go on, but I believe even as a woman, she hates women. She doesn't have an ounce of compassion, or bedside manner. Please avoid her at all costs. I will never get over how I've been treated by her.

one_star_reviews.text:
You're asking for something much more severe—something that communicates that, in your view, **management has allowed the institution to cease functioning as a proper library**. I can make it much sharper without weakening it with attacks based on nationality or homelessness itself.

What has happened to the Vancouver Public Library is an absolute disgrace.

This institution is called a public **library**, yet management appears to have abandoned even the most basic expectation associated with that word: providing an environment in which people can read, study, research, and work without being surrounded by constant noise, disorder, intoxication, and disruption.

The conditions I have repeatedly witnessed are unacceptable.

People conduct loud telephone conversations as though they were sitting in a coffee shop. Patrons openly talk at volumes completely inappropriate for a library. Even staff members engage in conversations loud enough to disturb people attempting to concentrate. Meanwhile, individuals who appear severely intoxicated or under the influence of drugs are routinely present, and behavior that should trigger immediate intervention seems instead to have become normalized.

Then there is security.

One security guard repeatedly bangs on washroom doors with an object during checks, creating an obnoxious noise that carries through the library. Think about the absurdity of that: the very people supposedly employed to maintain an orderly environment are themselves creating disturbances.

What exactly is management doing?

The problem is not that homeless people use the library. Homeless people have every right to use a public library **when they follow the same reasonable standards of behavior expected of everybody else**. The problem is allowing intoxication, drug-related behavior, excessive noise, disruption, and antisocial conduct to overwhelm the legitimate function of the building.

Compassion does not require turning a library into chaos.

Inclusiveness does not mean eliminating standards.

And tolerating virtually everything is not competent management.

At some point, Vancouver Public Library management needs to admit what this facility has become. Based on what I have repeatedly witnessed, it increasingly resembles a **poorly controlled drop-in center that happens to contain books**, rather than a professionally operated public library.

A library is not a homeless shelter.

It is not a detoxification center.

It is not a bar.

It is not a social club.

It is not a place where people should be free to shout across rooms or conduct loud telephone conversations.

And it certainly should not be a place where patrons attempting to study are expected to tolerate disruption created by the library's own security personnel.

**IT IS A LIBRARY.**

That distinction apparently needs to be rediscovered.

There are students trying to earn degrees. There are people researching, studying, applying for employment, learning new skills, reading, and trying to improve their lives. Some of those people have nowhere else suitable to work. Yet they are expected to tolerate an environment that management would presumably never accept in its own administrative offices.

Vancouver taxpayers fund this institution. They have every right to expect competent management, professional security, reasonable quiet, basic order, and behavioral standards that are actually enforced.

Stop pretending that enforcing reasonable standards is somehow incompatible with compassion.

Stop allowing disruptive behavior to dictate the environment for everyone else.

Stop expecting serious library users to simply tolerate it.

And start operating the Vancouver Public Library as an actual **library**.

Because right now, in my experience, it is failing at the most fundamental function contained in its own name.
Half a star.

one_star_reviews.text:
CPAP therapy is a medical treatment that requires active clinical monitoring to be safe and effective. Unfortunately, I spent five years as a patient here assuming someone was checking my data, only to find out otherwise.

This year I requested my file through a formal records request. In writing, the privacy office confirmed they have ‘no record of any internal incident reports, risk management reviews, quality assurance investigations or clinical audits’ related to my care, no record of any compliance alerts ever generated by my device despite years of concerning data, and that they ‘[do] not designate specific employees to manage care.’ No review of my file occurred at any point across five years — I only found out because I asked.

At no point in those five years was a Registered Respiratory Therapist ever involved in reviewing or overseeing my care — despite the fact that adjusting CPAP pressure settings is a controlled act in Ontario that's supposed to require exactly that kind of oversight. This wasn't a paperwork technicality: it had a real, negative impact on my quality of life over years I can't get back.

I'm deeply concerned about the lack of clinical oversight they've admitted to in writing. Improper or unmonitored CPAP use can have serious health consequences, and it appears no one was checking to catch that.
I've since switched providers and finally have regular clinical follow-up. If you're a patient here, it may be worth requesting your own file.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with my experience at Gold’s Gym.

English is not my first language, and when I signed up, I did not fully understand that I was being locked into a one-year contract. I feel that my limited English was not properly taken into consideration and the terms were not clearly explained to me.

Unfortunately, because of serious back and neck problems, I was only able to use the gym for about two weeks. Even after I stopped going, I continued making payments for several months.

I also provided medical documentation explaining that I was unable to continue using the gym because of my condition. Despite this, they are now demanding approximately $904 from me and continuing collection activity that is affecting my credit.

I tried to explain my situation and provided medical proof, but I do not feel that I have been treated fairly or reasonably.

Based on my personal experience, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering joining this gym carefully read every part of the membership agreement before signing, especially the cancellation policy and length of the contract.

When I got my membership there, they gave me a few one-day passes to use for my friends who are thinking of trying out the gym. When my gf drove all the way there last night to use the pass, they rejected her entry, saying she needs the manager’s approval. Well, maybe you should’ve put that disclaimer on the pass or let me know when you gave them to me instead of disrespecting other people’s time like this.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am a regular Domino’s Pizza customer. I usually order online through the Domino’s app, and I have never had any problems with my orders or service before. Unfortunately, my experience at this particular location was completely different.
We came as a family with two small children and placed our pizza order online. We were told the pizza would be ready within 10–15 minutes. We returned after about 15 minutes, expecting our order to be ready.
When we arrived, they initially tried to give me a pizza that I had NOT ordered, under a different name. I told them that this was not my order and that I had ordered a different pizza.
Only then did they tell me that they had “three Nathans” and that they didn't know where my pizza was. There was no apology, no proper explanation, and no attempt to take responsibility for the mistake.
Our two young children were hungry, and we had to wait another 10 minutes for our actual pizza. Even during that additional wait, there was no apology or acknowledgment of the inconvenience.
I understand that mistakes and delays can happen, especially when a location is busy. But giving a customer the wrong pizza under someone else's name, then saying you don't know where their actual order is, and showing absolutely no concern or apology is unacceptable customer service.
I have been a regular Domino’s customer and have ordered online many times without any issues. Unfortunately, this particular branch gave us a completely different experience.
Very disappointing. I hope management takes this feedback seriously, because this is not the level of service I expect from Domino’s.

It gets worse, 3:15 was our scheduled return time, you would think after the mornings debacle the driver would be on time for our return trip.NOPE!!   3:20 rolls around so I phoned to see where he was, he was just leaving the west end and we are downtown.  We had to load my father in law who can’t walk into our vehicle because we had many other things to do and could not wait any longer.  What is the purpose of booking times if they can’t honour the system?  Honestly you’d probably be better off to use your wheelchair to where you have to go because you would get there before they show up for their scheduled pick up time.  This company is an absolute joke and I would avoid them at all costs.  If I could give negative stars I would.

one_star_reviews.text: Long overdue:  A few years ago we took their 21 day "Australian Safari" Tour.  In spite of being on a bus that held 40 people even though we really would've preferred a small group tour, this could have been a nice tour. The problem was the tour guide.  She was cute looking, very energetic and knowledgeable, able to handle problems with flights and such as they arose, however, she was a very nasty human being.  From the get-go she made it clear she really didn't enjoy our "stupid" questions.   We and others according to her asked the wrong questions at the wrong time.  We got to a point where we simply stopped talking to her at all, which is what she seemed to want.   Little by little she formed her own subgroup and would make fun of people she didn't like with her subgroup.   We had never met a tour guide who rather than creating a cohesive and enjoyable time actively seemed to enjoy attacking people and isolating different people within the group.  Did she pull the wool over the GLOBUS executives?   I wrote to Global about this and they had nothing to say whatsoever and buried the review completely.  They said the reviews we wrote were for internal use only.  I have no idea if this same tour guide is still working for them.  We would like to think that she was fired immediately, but I have no idea.  We would never go on another Global trip... and we spend a lot of money traveling so don't want to take a second chance on another very disturbing and upsetting trip that we spent a great deal of money on.  Imagine, 21 days with this very nasty human being.  It just got worse and worse as the days went on.  She actively encouraged her "chosen ones" to say nasty things about people.  Amazing.

one_star_reviews.text:
Riipen is a platform that connects students with short-term, paid projects so they can gain real work experience, build their resumes and learn in a professional environment. I had completed multiple projects through Riipen before this one and had genuinely positive experiences, so I was excited to join the February 2026 cohort. I specifically chose this project because it was centered around empowering young women.

Unfortunately, my experience with Gina (the owner) and Radiant Girls was completely different. From the very beginning, Gina created a pressuring and threatening environment that felt completely inappropriate for a student learning opportunity. Rather than using the program as an opportunity to help students learn, collaborate and grow, I felt that the system was being used to pressure students into meeting her expectations through repeated references to removal and the possibility of losing future opportunities.

It was so concerning that three women on our team ultimately left within the first week. That was completely out of the ordinary compared with my previous Riipen experiences. What stood out to me was that this did not feel like a normal difference in working styles. It felt like students were being put under unnecessary pressure from the start, and several of us independently reached the same conclusion that the environment was not something we wanted to continue in.

What made the situation even worse was Gina’s response afterward. She left comments suggesting that I had simply “disappeared” and failed to communicate, despite the fact that I had clearly explained my reasons for leaving. I found that incredibly disappointing, especially after feeling that the communication throughout the project had been threatening in the first place. There also appeared to be an attempt to make students feel that leaving this project could affect whether we received future opportunities through the platform. The irony is that the threats didn't work- I continued using Riipen, completed another project successfully, and have continued building my experience. Apparently leaving one unhealthy project didn't end my career after all.

I am also aware that reports have been made to Riipen regarding this organization and are currently under review. I obviously cannot speak to the outcome of those reports, but I think students deserve to know that concerns have been raised.

What I find most disappointing is the disconnect between this experience and what Radiant Girls is supposed to represent. An organization centered around empowering young women should be creating an environment where young women feel respected, supported and encouraged to grow. My experience felt like the opposite. I think that is especially important for students and parents to consider when deciding who they trust with young people.

Riipen itself has been an incredibly valuable platform for me, and I have had opportunities through it that genuinely helped me grow. My issue is not with Riipen. It is with organizations and project leads who, in my opinion, take advantage of a program that is supposed to help students learn and gain experience, rather than making students feel intimidated or disposable.

Students, especially young women, should read the existing reviews and make sure they are comfortable with the environment before getting involved with Radiant Girls.

I used to visit this place frequently and genuinely enjoyed the food. Unfortunately, I recently broke my right foot and, having carelessly failed to employ a private chauffeur to collect my takeout, I subscribed to Uber Eats.

I ordered a chicken shawarma salad with added falafel and paid for extra chicken, plus a beef shawarma salad with extra potatoes. What arrived was two falafels instead of three and a chicken shawarma salad featuring an exciting game of “Find the Chicken.”

I understand that Uber takes a commission and the restaurant earns less than it does from walk-in customers. That is precisely why I paid for extra meat—naively expecting to receive at least the equivalent of a regular portion. Instead, I paid extra and received less. Apparently, “extra chicken” means the chicken receives extra time off.

Unless the restaurant can demonstrate that the portions were correct—perhaps with time-stamped photos showing the complete contents of my order—this was my final order from them. It is unfortunate, because I enjoyed supporting this business in person. Evidently, customers ordering through Uber Eats are served a different standard: higher prices, smaller portions, and a complimentary lesson in lowered expectations.

Or maybe Uber diver ate missing stuff?

I reached out to Forest Hill Center urgently seeking therapy support for my son during a difficult time. We specifically requested cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and were matched with a clinician recommended as a suitable fit.

Unfortunately, the booking and matching process was disappointing. Our first introductory call was delayed by 25 minutes, the rescheduled call did not take place because the clinician did not attend, and we were subsequently informed that the clinician did not offer CBT, the service we had requested from the outset.

My concern is with the centre’s process for confirming that a clinician offers the requested treatment before recommending them and scheduling appointments. Clear communication about services and reliable scheduling are especially important when families are seeking timely support for a child. The time spent waiting could have been used to pursue care elsewhere.

I do want to acknowledge that the practice communicated with me several times, offered recommendations, and made efforts to address the situation. They also reached out following my original review. I appreciate those efforts and have updated this review accordingly.

While that follow-up is appreciated, it does not change the difficulties we experienced. I hope the centre strengthens its booking, matching, and communication practices so other families can access appropriate care without unnecessary delays.

My daughter was briefly a client at this practice (which I had arranged). They are new to my area and in a convenient location but my daughter said the overall vibe felt off after her visit. She said it felt very slick and not authentic. This  prompted me to do some further research. I  mentioned her to a friend who suggested we look at Dr. Bot's social media posts  including looking at her Twitter. I  We then looked at her profile—something I  had wished we  had done first. As a woman, I was taken aback to see that she posts in support of people like Jordan Peterson and Pierre Poilievre, two extremely misogynist figures who believe men are the victims in most female traumas. She can believe whatever she wants, but these are alarming views for someone offering mental health services for young women to publicize. This is extremely triggering and the opposite of what a mental health professional should be putting out there. I’m glad I did my due diligence, wish I had done so before her appointment.

Update- May 31, 2025
Yes, I just looked as I saw there was a response and I see that in the year and a half since I posted my review that Dr. Bot has now created a new Twitter account following lots of “woke” profiles. These are not the people she was following at the time my daughter saw her. She has definitely cleaned up her social media account in response to my review. I think this is the definition of gaslighting—that’s really something for a therapist to do.

Update: It's amazing how many reviews popped up at the same time 2 months ago to counter my review. I would take them with a grain of salt. And now my review has disappeared yet again!! Why is this happening? Is Forest Hill Centre getting it taken down?

Title: 6-week project has taken over a year. Unacceptable delays and zero communication.
I am extremely frustrated with Russ Pet Construction. My condo board hired them for a 6-week contract to replace two retaining walls on our condo property in 2025. We are now over 52 weeks into the project—an entire year later—and the work is still not completed.
To be fair, the retaining walls themselves appear to be built quite well, and the actual quality of the craftsmanship looks good. However, the logistical management of this project has been a complete nightmare.
Because this project has dragged on for over a year, some residents have lost access to backyards and vital parking for countless weeks. On top of losing parking, the crew has left a persistent, disruptive mess across our property. Taking over a year to finish a 6-week  project can't be blamed on the rain... I  cannot recommend this company for any project.
